title: Set a block down 10 cm beyond a taped line, measuring with a ruler
instruction: put the block down with its centre 10 cm beyond the red line
context: Layout work, from setting out fixtures to spacing parts on a bench, means placing things a measured distance from a reference line. A robot that places things 'about there' fails it; here it can use the ruler on the table.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Line: red tape 6 mm wide and 50 cm long, flat on the table, fixed, square to the midline, its centre line 12 cm forward. (2) Ruler: a white strip 4.5 cm wide and 22 cm long, flat on the table, fixed, running forward from the tape's centre line, centred 15 cm left; black ticks along its right edge every centimetre (1 cm long) and every 5 cm (2 cm long), with 5, 10, 15 and 20 printed beside the long ticks. (3) Block: a blue wooden block, a 4 cm cube, 40 g, loose, 7 cm forward and 10 cm right. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. The error is how far the block's centre is from 10 cm beyond the tape's centre line, measured square to the tape; its sideways position doesn't matter. The block must rest on the table (its centre no more than 2.8 cm above it; on the ruler counts). 1.0: error 1 cm or less. 0.5: error 2 cm or less. 0.0: a larger error, or not resting on the table.
reset_notes: Put the block back 7 cm forward and 10 cm right. The tape and ruler are fixed.
fidelity: Calibrated YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The tape and ruler are fixed flat strips; the ticks and numbers are 1 mm raised black strips (printed in the real world). The block is a rigid cube of the stated size and mass. Lighting and cameras follow the station calibration.
